subject: Bridge pricing + commit realignment proposal
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@nimbushealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal question — short gap in commit coverage

Hi Alex / Marissa,

Quick context: we’re finalizing our budget but our Q4 usage ramped faster than expected — we’ll exceed our committed monthly tokens by about ~35% this month. Procurement is asking whether Redwood can provide a short-term bridge (credits or a temporary per-token cap) while we finalize the next quarter’s commit. We’re not looking to renegotiate the full term yet, just a way to avoid surprise overage billing for December and give us time to right-size for the renewal.

Also curious about any limits on renewal uplift — last cycle we had a 30% step-up and that made forecasting tricky for us. Can you outline options (credits, temporary per-token caps, or a phased commit) and any constraints on uplift percentage?

We have a renewal target date of 2027-01-15.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Director of ML Engineering, NimbusHealth
 Attachments: Nimbus_usage_export.csv (stub)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@nimbushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc:  Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal question — short gap in commit coverage

Hi Daniel — thanks for the heads up and the usage export. Short answer: yes, we can do a short bridge while we lock in the renewal. I’ve sketched two practical options below (high level) and attached the downloadable pricing worksheet so you can see the numbers.

Option A — Bridge credit + true-up
- Redwood issues a one-time bridge credit that covers estimated overage through 2026-12-31.
- Client signs a small interim true-up commitment (1-month lookback) that will be applied toward the 2027 commit if renewed.
- No change to per-token tiers for active month; true-up converts to committed dollars at renewal.

Option B — Temporary per-token cap + phased commit
- We cap per-token effective rate for December at a pre-agreed floor (e.g., current blended rate).
- We propose a phased commit: Q1 commit = 70% of expected run-rate, with a 90-day true-up window and a maximum renewal uplift cap of 20% vs current baseline.

Questions for you: do you prefer a credit (A) or a capped per-token approach (B)? I can route to finance for a quick approval if you indicate a preference.

Next steps: I’ve attached a short worksheet (redwood_bridge_pricing_sheet.xlsx) with example math and a draft SOW placeholder. If that looks right I’ll pull Marissa and Ben in to finalize terms and DocuSign.

Available for a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon if helpful.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0142
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal question — short gap in commit coverage (pricing ask)

Marissa / Ben / Karthik — looping you in for quick pricing guidance. Client prefers minimal admin — likely prefers Option B (per-token cap) but flagged renewal uplift as a major stakeholder concern. Key numbers from the worksheet (approx):
- Current blended per-token (effective): $0.0009/token
- Dec estimated overage: 35% of committed tokens -> ~1.1B tokens
- Proposed temporary cap: $0.00095/token for Dec (essentially current blended)
- Phased Q1 commit: 70% run-rate with 90d true-up
- Proposed uplift cap: 20% max at renewal (absolute, not compounded)

Finance sign-off needed on: 1) approving temporary cap through month-end, 2) allowing uplift cap <=20% as an exception to standard maximum.

If we approve, I’ll send the formal proposal and attach SOW stub.

— Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T10:34:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Renewal question — short gap in commit coverage (proposal)

Thanks Alex — reviewed with finance. We can sign off on a limited bridge with the following guardrails: 

Formal proposal (what we'll offer to NimbusHealth):
1) Short-term per-token cap for December 2026: cap effective rate at $0.00095/token covering overage through 2026-12-31.
2) Phased Q1 commit: Client to commit to 70% of projected run-rate for Q1 2027. True-up window: 90 days post-quarter to reconcile usage.
3) Renewal uplift guardrail: max 20% uplift to per-token list rates compared to NimbusHealth’s current baseline. Any uplift above 20% requires VP-level approval and a 30-day prior notice window.
4) One-time bridge credit: if December overage is less than estimated, remaining balance auto-applies toward Q1 committed spend.
5) Documentation: we’ll prepare an interim SOW and DocuSign link. Billing will reflect capped rate for December and true-up adjustments per the SOW.

Attachments: redwood_bridge_pricing_sheet.xlsx (detailed math)
Links: DocuSign SOW draft (will send in separate email)

Marissa — please confirm you’re OK to include the 20% uplift cap explicitly. Ben / Karthik: any objections on accounting treatment / recognition for ARR?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

Please send the interim SOW + DocuSign and confirm that the capped billing rate applies for December usage while we complete the renewal.
